findings.source_quote: ὅτι ἔχοντες ζωὴν εἰς θάνατον ἑαυτοὺς παραδεδώκασι.
findings.english_quote: because, though they had life, they have handed themselves over to death.
findings.issue: The present participle ἔχοντες describes having life, not merely having had it previously. The English introduces a past-versus-present contrast that the selected source does not state.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “because, though they have life, they have handed themselves over to death.”

findings.source_quote: ἄκουε οὖν, [φησί,] καθὼς βούλει, ἵνα νοήσῃς αὐτά.
findings.english_quote: Listen then,” he says, “as you desire, so that you may understand these things.
findings.issue: The English presents “he says” without disclosing that this occurrence of φησί is bracketed as an editorial supplement in the selected working source. The speaker identification is compatible with the context, but the distinction between supplied and preserved wording is lost.
findings.suggested_revision: Disclose in a source note that this “he says” represents bracketed editorial wording in the selected source, or omit the supplied phrase while retaining clear dialogue attribution. Any revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Ὅτι, φημί, κύριε, οὐ νενόηκα ὅλως περὶ τοῦ χρόνου τῆς ἀπάτης καὶ τρυφῆς καὶ βασάνου, τηλαυγέστερόν μοι δήλωσον.
findings.english_quote: “Since,” I say, “sir,[6] I have not understood at all about the time of deception and delight[1] and torment,[2] make it more plain to me.”
findings.issue: The text contains numbered note calls [1] through [6], but the supplied footnotes contain only marker “a.” These dangling calls prevent readers from accessing the apparent explanations or source-choice disclosures. Marker [6] also occurs at two unrelated locations, without an available note establishing its intended scope.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply the actual numbered notes and verify their correspondence to every call, including both occurrences of [6], or remove obsolete calls if no notes are intended. The missing notes cannot be presumed correct or reconstructed from the markers.

findings.source_quote: οὐ νενόηκα ὅλως περὶ τοῦ χρόνου τῆς ἀπάτης καὶ τρυφῆς καὶ βασάνου
findings.english_quote: I do not understand the period of deception, self-indulgence, and torment.
findings.issue: The explicit totalizing emphasis ὅλως, “at all,” is omitted. This reduces the stated extent of the speaker’s failure to understand.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “I do not understand at all the period of deception, pleasure, and torment.” Review the rendering of τρυφή together with its later positive uses.

findings.source_quote: ἄκουε οὖν, [φησί,] καθὼς βούλει, ἵνα νοήσῃς αὐτά.
findings.english_quote: If you want to understand these things, listen.
findings.issue: The source directs him to listen as he desires, for the purpose of understanding. The English replaces that structure with an unstated conditional and omits the explicit acknowledgment “as you desire.”
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “So listen, as you wish, so that you can understand these things.” The bracketed speech tag may be omitted without treating it as preserved wording.

findings.source_quote: βασανιζόμενος οὖν καὶ τιμωρούμενος ὅλον τὸν ἐνιαυτὸν μνημονεύει ποτὲ τῆς τρυφῆς καὶ ἀπάτης
findings.english_quote: So, while he is tormented and punished for a whole year, he remembers his self-indulgence and the deception.
findings.issue: The temporal qualification ποτὲ is omitted. The English gives unqualified remembering rather than remembering at some point or eventually during the punishment.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “So, while he is tormented and punished for a whole year, he eventually remembers his pleasure and deception.” Confirm the temporal wording and the consistent pleasure terminology in the next review.

findings.source_quote: πᾶς οὖν ἄνθρωπος ὁ τρυφῶν καὶ ἀπατώμενος οὕτω βασανίζεται, ὅτι ἔχοντες ζωὴν εἰς θάνατον ἑαυτοὺς παραδεδώκασι.
findings.english_quote: Everyone who indulges himself and is deceived is tormented in this way. Although they have life, they have given themselves over to death.
findings.issue: The causal connection expressed by ὅτι is omitted. The source explains why these people are tormented; the English makes the surrender to death a separate assertion without explicitly preserving that explanation.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “Everyone who indulges himself and is deceived is tormented in this way because, although they have life, they have given themselves over to death.”

findings.source_quote: εἰσὶν δὲ καὶ τρυφαὶ σώζουσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους·
findings.english_quote: But some kinds of pleasure can also save people.
findings.issue: The added “can” weakens the assertion from pleasures that save people to pleasures merely capable of saving them. The selected source does not supply that qualification.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “But there are also pleasures that save people.”

findings.source_quote: αὕτη οὖν ἡ τρυφὴ σύμφορός ἐστι τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ζωὴν περιποιεῖται τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τοιούτῳ·
findings.english_quote: This kind of pleasure benefits the servants of God and brings such a person to life.
findings.issue: “Brings such a person to life” introduces a transition from being without life to becoming alive. The source says that this pleasure obtains or secures life for such a person; it does not specify that transition.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “This kind of pleasure benefits God’s servants and secures life for such a person.”

findings.source_quote: Πᾶσα, φησί, πρᾶξις τρυφή ἐστι τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, ὃ ἐὰν ἡδέως ποιῇ·
findings.english_quote: Every act that a person takes pleasure in is a form of self-indulgence.
findings.issue: Rendering τρυφή as “self-indulgence” in the general definition, but as “pleasure” in the saving examples, obscures the source’s deliberate use of the same term for harmful and beneficial enjoyment. “Self-indulgence” also imports a negative evaluation into the definition before the source distinguishes the two kinds. No lexical or simplification decision documents this variance.
findings.suggested_revision: Review a consistent rendering such as “pleasure” or “delight” across the definition and both categories. If contextual variation remains necessary, document it and preserve the shared source category explicitly rather than dividing it into inherently negative self-indulgence and positive pleasure.

findings.source_quote: εἰσὶν δὲ καὶ τρυφαὶ σώζουσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἀγαθὰ ἐργαζόμενοι τρυφῶσι τῇ ἑαυτῶν ἡδονῇ φερόμενοι.
findings.english_quote: But some kinds of pleasure can also save people. Many people please themselves by doing good and are carried along by the pleasure they find in it.
findings.issue: The simplified edition closes the teacher’s quotation before this paragraph and does not reopen it. It likewise leaves the preceding explanation beginning “A person who gives in to his desires” outside the quotation. Both passages remain part of the answering speaker’s discourse in the source, but the punctuation presents them as narrator exposition.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore consistent quotation boundaries showing that the answering speaker delivers sections 3–4 and the final paragraph, while preserving the intervening question by the first-person narrator. Review the complete dialogue punctuation after correction.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard largely preserves the selected source but has missing numbered notes, an undisclosed editorial speech-tag supplement, and a temporal shift in the life/death assertion. The simplified edition additionally loses qualifications and a causal connection, weakens the saving assertion, introduces a coming-to-life claim, obscures the shared pleasure terminology, and misattributes portions of the dialogue through quotation boundaries. Both use reader-facing “servants” and contextually appropriate “repent.” This review concerns only the supplied working source and English records; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify editions. All proposed corrections require fresh review.
